questions.qtext:
With respect to relational algebra, which of the following operations are included from mathematical set theory?

  1. Join
  2. Intersection
  3. Cartisian product
  4. Project
    1. i and iv
    2. ii and iii
    3. iii and iv
    4. ii and iv

options.text: Choose option A from the question above.
Choose option B from the question above.
Choose option C from the question above.
Choose option D from the question above.

questions.solution:
Answer: B

Selected solution (score: 2)
Answer is Option $\boxed{B}$

1. Join operation is not present in set theory.

2. Intersection: yes present in set theory

3. Cartesian product: yes present in set theory aswell.

4. Project operation: No, this is not present in set theory.

questions.qtext:
Given the relations

  • employee (name, salary, dept-no), and
  • department (dept-no, dept-name,address),

Which of the following queries cannot be expressed using the basic relational algebra operations $\left(\sigma, \pi,\times ,\Join, \cup, \cap,-\right)$?

options.text: Department address of every employee
Employees whose name is the same as their department name
The sum of all employees' salaries
All employees of a given department

questions.solution:
Answer: C

Source solution 1 (score: 1)
Correct Answer: C. The sum of all employees' salaries

This cannot be expressed using basic relational algebra because aggregation operations like SUM are not supported in the basic set of operations. Aggregation requires extended relational algebra or SQL.

Queries for the other options:

A. Department address of every employee

We can use a natural join or theta join on dept-no, then project the needed attributes.

π_name, address (employee ⨝ department)

B. Employees whose name is the same as their department name

This compares two attributes (from different relations), which is allowed using a theta join and a selection condition.

π_name (σ_name = dept-name (employee × department))

D. All employees of a given department

Assuming the department is known (say dept-no = 10):

σ_dept-no = 10 (employee)

questions.qtext:
Consider the relations $R(A, B)$ and $S(B, C)$ and the following four relational algebra queries over R ans S

  1. $\pi_{A, B} (R \bowtie S)$
  2. $R \bowtie \pi_B(S)$
  3. $R \cap (\pi_A(R) \times \pi_B (S))$
  4. $\Pi_{A. R. B} (R \times S)$ where $R.B$ refers to the column B in table R

One can determine that:

options.text: I, III and IV are the same query
II, III and IV are the same query
I, II and IV are the same query
I, II and III are the same query

questions.solution:
Answer: D

Selected solution (score: 3)

Answer is option $\boxed{D}$

Lets understand each query.

I. $\pi_{A,B}(R\bowtie S )$

Perform natural join on R and S and then select Columns A and B from it.

Here we are outputing all those tuples of Relation $R(A,B)$ for which the attribute $R.B$ value is present in $S.B$

II. $R\bowtie \pi_B (S)$

We are doing natural join with only column S.B.

This will also give is all those tuple of Relation $R(A,B)$ for which the attribute $R.B$ value is present in $S.B$

III. $R \cap (\pi_A(R) \times \pi_B(S))$

First we are doing cross product of all values of $A$ present in $R$ with all value of $B$ present in $S$ and then taking intersection with $R$. Which will again give us all those tuple of Relation $R(A,B)$ for which the attribute $R.B$ value is present in $S.B$

IV. $\prod_{A,R.B}(R\times S)$

This will give some extra tuples aswell.

Example:

R(A,B)
AB
12
14

S(B,C)
BC
210

perform $R\times S$ and then select columns $A$ and $R.B$ we will get
AB
12
14
Which is wrong .
Correct result should have been
AB
12

Hence only statements $I, II$ and $III$ are equivalent.
